clues.text: This town sits in a narrow river valley in the north of Turkey. It lies just inland from the Black Sea shore.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside northern Turkey near the Black Sea

source.quote: Amasya stands in the mountains above the Black Sea (Karadeniz) coast, set apart from the rest of Anatolia in a narrow valley along the banks of the Yeşilırmak (Iris) River.

clues.text: It sits high above the sea that lies close by. So it has an inland climate, not a coast one, and its air suits apple trees.
clues.narrowing: rules out low coastal towns in the region; points to a high inland valley

source.quote: Although near the Black Sea, this area is high above the coast and has an inland climate, well-suited to growing apples, for which Amasya province, one of the provinces in north-central Anatolia Turkey, is famed.

clues.text: In old Ottoman times, young princes were sent here to rule. They came to learn and gain skill before they might rule the whole land.
clues.narrowing: rules out towns never used to train Ottoman princes

source.quote: During the early Ottoman rule, it was customary for young Ottoman princes to be sent to Amasya to govern and gain experience.

clues.text: Look up from the old wood homes by the river. High on the cliffs you can see tombs cut for kings of old.
clues.narrowing: near-decisive; cliff tombs of kings above a river town are rare

source.quote: With its Ottoman-period wooden houses and the tombs of the Pontus kings carved into the cliffs overhead, Amasya is attractive to visitors.

clues.text: Old Ottoman wood houses line the banks of the river. Now they serve as cafes and inns where guests can eat and rest.
clues.narrowing: confirms the river town famed for its restored Ottoman houses

source.quote: Traditional Ottoman houses near the Yeşilırmak and the other main historical buildings have been restored; these traditional Yalıboyu houses are now used as cafes, restaurants, pubs and hotels.
